native.admission_inspect: A small paper tag, creased once. Both faces read THIS SIDE UP. They cannot both be.
apply_texts: You set the tag the first way. Leaving it and turning it feel equally finished.
You turn it and the instruction is already satisfied. The ease is small and poorly earned.
You turn it as though starting. The crease was already waiting on the far side.
You turn it back. It was already that way. The fold disagrees, without raising its voice.
You turn it back. The words stay. You are the part that does not match the instruction.
You turn it. The sentence is identical, which is not the same thing as unchanged.
You turn the tag. THIS SIDE UP meets you again. This side is cooler, which settles nothing.
inspect_texts: A small paper tag, creased once. Both faces read THIS SIDE UP. They cannot both be.
Back to the first face, or a face like it. THIS SIDE UP has not chosen a side.
It is crease-up again, if again is the word. Both ups remain, and neither yields.
Only paper. Read twice, each face denies the position that would make the other true.
Ordinary paper, one crease. Each face claims to be up, so neither claim can stand.
The same line faces you. You are less sure which side was up before the turn.
Turned over, it still reads THIS SIDE UP. The paper is cooler. The crease points down.
native.name: The Twice-Faced Tag
